examples.dm: Homage to all buddhas and bodhisattvas.
examples.gm: Homage to all the buddhas and bodhisattvas.

examples.dm: Just as a flash of lightning in the darkness of a cloud-shrouded night Momentarily reveals everything in its brilliant light, So too, through the power of the Buddha, A virtuous mind occasionally and briefly arises in the world.
examples.gm: Just as on a dark night in the womb of clouds A flash of lightning brilliantly illuminates for an instant, In the same way, by the power of the Buddha, occasionally Worldly intelligence for merit arises for a moment.
examples.sa: रात्रौ यथा मेघघनान्धकारे विद्युत् क्षणं दर्शयति प्रकाशम्। बुद्धानुभावेन तथा कदाचि-ल्लोकस्य पुण्येषु मतिः क्षणं स्यात्॥

examples.dm: By reflecting in this way, one should maintain A sense of shame, respect, and likewise fear. Consequently, the recollection of the Buddha Will also arise in one again and again.
examples.gm: Thinking like this, with shame, Respect, and fear, one should dwell. Thus, the recollection of the Buddhas, Will also arise in one again and again.
examples.sa: इति ध्यात्वा तथा तिष्ठेत् त्रपादरभयान्वितः। बुद्धानुस्मृतिरप्येवं भवेत्तस्य मुहुर्मुहुः॥

examples.dm: All other virtues are like the plantain tree; Once they have produced their fruit, they are exhausted. But the tree of the awakening mind perpetually bears fruit, And rather than being exhausted, it increases ever more.
examples.gm: All other virtues are just like the plantain tree: Having borne their fruit, they are exhausted; But the tree of the mind of awakening constantly Bears fruit, is not exhausted, and continually grows.
examples.sa: कदलीव फलं विहाय याति क्षयमन्यत् कुशलं हि सर्वमेव। सततं फलति क्षयं न याति प्रसवत्येव तु बोधिचित्तवृक्षः॥

examples.dm: Although great fruits arise from the aspiring mind While wandering in cyclic existence, It does not produce a continuous flow of merit In the way that the engaging mind does.
examples.gm: From the mind aspiring to awakening, Great fruits arise while in cyclic existence, but Unlike the mind entering awakening, A continuous stream of merit does not arise.
examples.sa: बोधिप्रणिधिचित्तस्य संसारेऽपि फलं महत्। न त्वविच्छिन्नपुण्यत्वं यथा प्रस्थानचेतसः॥

examples.dm: Just as the result of generating a single clear mind Is birth as a Brahmā or the like, The results of body and speech are not such, Because their conduct is weak.
examples.gm: Whatever result is generated by a single clear mind, Such as Brahmā and so forth, The results of body and speech, Because of weak conduct, are not like that.
examples.sa: सहापि वाक्शरीराभ्यां मन्दवृत्तेर्न तत्फलम्। यत्पटोरेककस्यापि चित्तस्य ब्रह्मतादिकम्॥

examples.dm: It is the universal bridge that delivers All beings from the lower realms; It is the rising moon of the mind that dispels The heat of the afflictions of all beings.
examples.gm: For all wandering beings, from the lower realms It is the universal bridge that liberates. Dispelling the torment of the afflictions of wandering beings, It is the rising moon of the mind.
examples.sa: दुर्गत्युत्तरणे सेतुः सामान्यः सर्वयायिनाम्। जगत्क्लेशोपशमन उदितश्चित्तचन्द्रमाः॥

examples.dm: Anyone who, even for a single moment, Creates obstacles or hinders this merit, Diminishes the welfare of sentient beings, And for them, rebirth in lower realms is endless.
examples.gm: Whoever else, even for a mere moment, Creates an obstacle to this merit, Because the benefit of sentient beings is diminished, Their lower rebirths will be limitless.
examples.sa: योऽप्यन्यः क्षणमप्यस्य पुण्यविघ्नं करिष्यति। तस्य दुर्गतिपर्यन्तो नास्ति सत्त्वार्थघातिनः॥

examples.dm: One who desires high status for oneself Will be reborn in the lower realms, in wretchedness, and as a fool. If that very desire is transferred to others, One will attain good migrations and be honored.
examples.gm: Through wishing for oneself to be exalted, One will fall to bad migrations and become base and foolish. If that very thing is shifted to others, One will obtain happy migrations and respect.
examples.sa: दुर्गतिर्नीचता मौर्ख्यं ययैवात्मोन्नतीच्छया। तामेवान्यत्र संक्राम्य सुगतिः सत्कृतिर्मतिः॥

examples.dm: To the Victors who intend to pass into nirvana, I join my palms and pray: Do not leave these beings in blindness, But please remain for countless eons.
examples.gm: To the Conquerors wishing to pass into nirvana, With joined palms I pray: So as not to leave these wanderers in blindness, I beseech you to remain for countless eons.
examples.sa: निर्वातुकामांश्च जिनान् याचयामि कृताञ्जलिः। कल्पाननन्तांस्तिष्ठन्तु मा भूदन्धमिदं जगत्॥

examples.dm: So too, for the benefit of all beings, Shall I generate the mind of enlightenment, And likewise, in those trainings, I shall train in successive order.
examples.gm: Likewise, for the benefit of wandering beings, I shall generate the awakening mind, And likewise, in the trainings too, I shall progressively train.
examples.sa: तद्वदुत्पादयाम्येष बोधिचित्तं जगद्धिते। तद्वदेव च ताः शिक्षाः शिक्षिष्यामि यथाक्रमम्॥

examples.dm: If you do not wish for them to have even this, How can you wish for them to attain enlightenment? Where is the bodhicitta in one Who becomes angry at the prosperity of others?
examples.gm: If you do not want this for wandering beings, How can you desire awakening for them? For one who is angry at another's prosperity, Where is the mind of awakening?
examples.sa: स किं नेच्छसि सत्त्वानां यस्तेषां बोधिमिच्छति। बोधिचित्तं कुतस्तस्य योऽन्यसंपदि कुप्यति॥

examples.dm: I am destitute and lack merit, And have no other wealth for making offerings. Therefore, O Protectors who care for the welfare of others, Please accept this through your own power for my sake.
examples.gm: I am without merit and extremely destitute, And I have no other wealth for offering. Therefore, may the Protectors whose thoughts are for the welfare of others, By their own power, accept this for my sake.
examples.sa: अपुण्यवानस्मि महादरिद्रः पूजार्थमन्यन्मम नास्ति किंचित्। अतो ममार्थाय परार्थचित्ता गृह्णन्तु नाथा इदमात्मशक्त्या॥

examples.dm: When the intention to neglect the welfare of others, Or the desire to pursue one's own interests, Or the urge to speak arises, At those times, one should remain like a log of wood.
examples.gm: Forsaking the benefit of others, And desiring to pursue one's own benefit, If a mind desiring to speak arises, Because of that, one should remain like a piece of wood.
examples.sa: परार्थरूक्षं स्वार्थार्थि परिषत्काममेव वा। वक्तुमिच्छति मे चित्तं तस्मात्तिष्ठामि काष्ठवत्॥

examples.dm: If the body is at ease through merit, And the mind is at ease through wisdom, Then even while remaining in samsara for the sake of others, Why would those with compassion ever be weary?
examples.gm: Through merit, the body is at ease, And through wisdom, the mind is at ease. Even while remaining in cyclic existence for the sake of others, Why would the compassionate ones become weary?
examples.sa: पुण्येन कायः सुखितः पाण्डित्येन मनः सुखि। तिष्ठन् परार्थं संसारे कृपालुः केन खिद्यते॥

examples.dm: I prostrate to the foundations of the awakening mind and to the reliquaries; I prostrate to the preceptors, the masters, And to those who maintain the supreme ascetic discipline.
examples.gm: To the bases of the awakening mind, And to the stūpas, I pay homage. To the preceptors and likewise the teachers, And to the supreme practitioners, I pay homage.
examples.sa: सर्वचैत्यानि वन्देऽहं बोधिसत्त्वाश्रयांस्तथा। नमः करोम्युपाध्यायानभिवन्द्यान् यतींस्तथा॥

examples.dm: Through associating with a spiritual master, Following the instructions of a preceptor, And through fear, the fortunate who act with respect Will easily develop mindfulness.
examples.gm: From associating with gurus, And the instructions of preceptors, In the fortunate who act with respect out of fear, Mindfulness is easily generated.
examples.sa: उपाध्यायानुशासन्या भीत्याप्यादरकारिणाम्। धन्यानां गुरुसंवासात्सुकरं जायते स्मृतिः॥

examples.dm: This was translated, edited, and finalized from a Kashmiri manuscript by the Indian scholar Sarvajñādeva and the chief editor-translator Bandé Paltseg.
examples.gm: Revised and finalized by the Indian preceptor Sarvajñādeva and the chief editor-translator, the monk Paltsek, based on a Kashmiri manuscript;

examples.dm: The worldly perceive things and conceptualize them As being truly real, rather than like an illusion; It is on this point that The yogis and the worldly dispute.
examples.gm: People of the world see entities, And conceptualize them as truly real, Not as being like illusions; therefore, here, Yogis and the world dispute.
examples.sa: लोकेन भावा दृश्यन्ते कल्प्यन्ते चापि तत्त्वतः। न तु मायावदित्यत्र विवादो योगिलोकयोः॥

examples.dm: Since a non-entity depends upon an entity, How could it possess the capacity for action? Your mind would then be without any companion, It would become entirely solitary.
examples.gm: "Since a non-entity depends on a real entity, How could it be endowed with a function?" Your mind, being without a companion, Would become entirely alone.
examples.sa: वस्त्वाश्रयेणाभावस्य क्रियावत्त्वं कथं भवेत्। असत्सहायमेकं हि चित्तमापद्यते तव॥

examples.dm: When neither entities nor non-entities Remain before the mind, Then, since there is no other aspect, It is thoroughly pacified in non-apprehension.
examples.gm: When both entities and non-entities Do not remain before the mind, At that time, since there is no other aspect, It is completely pacified, without an object of focus.
examples.sa: यदा न भावो नाभावो मतेः संतिष्ठते पुरः। तदान्यगत्यभावेन निरालम्बा प्रशाम्यति॥

examples.dm: Overwhelmed by the confusion of ignorance, And whatever I have rejoiced in— Having seen those faults, I confess them to the Protectors from the depths of my heart.
examples.gm: And, overcome by the confusion of ignorance, Whatever I have rejoiced in, Having seen these mistakes, I confess them to the Protectors from the depths of my heart.
examples.sa: यच्चानुमोदितं किंचिदात्मघाताय मोहतः। तदत्ययं देशयामि पश्चात्तापेन तापितः॥

examples.dm: Whatever sins I, a sinner stained by many faults, Have committed through my many transgressions, Those extremely unbearable deeds, I confess to all the Guides.
examples.gm: Defiled by many faults, Whatever non-virtues I, a sinner, Have committed that are extremely unbearable, I confess them all to the Guides.
examples.sa: अनेकदोषदुष्टेन मया पापेन नायकाः। यत्कृतं दारुणं पापं तत्सर्वं देशयाम्यहम्॥

examples.dm: In the presence of the Protectors, openly, With palms joined and a mind fearful of suffering, I prostrate again and again, And I confess all of these.
examples.gm: Directly in the presence of the protectors, With palms joined and a mind terrified of suffering, Bowing down again and again, I will confess all of them.
examples.sa: तत्सर्वं देशयाम्येष नाथानामग्रतः स्थितः। कृताञ्जलिर्दुःखभीतः प्रणिपत्य पुनः पुनः॥

examples.dm: Thus, it is not reasonable To direct refutations toward the position of emptiness. Therefore, without harboring any doubt, One should meditate upon emptiness.
examples.gm: Thus, toward the side of emptiness, Refutation is not appropriate. Therefore, without hesitation, One should meditate on emptiness.
examples.sa: तदेवं शून्यतापक्षे दूषणं नोपपद्यते। तस्मान्निर्विचिकित्सेन भावनीयैव शून्यता॥

examples.dm: Emptiness is the antidote To the darkness of the afflictive and cognitive obscurations. Why, then, would those who desire to swiftly attain omniscience Not meditate upon it?
examples.gm: Of the obscurations of afflictions and knowables, Emptiness is the antidote to the darkness. By one who wishes to quickly become omniscient, How could one not meditate on it?
examples.sa: क्लेशज्ञेयावृतितमःप्रतिपक्षो हि शून्यता। शीघ्रं सर्वज्ञताकामो न भावयति तां कथम्॥

examples.dm: If a valid authority is not valid, Would that which is measured by it not be false? In that case, the meditation On emptiness would be untenable.
examples.gm: If valid cognition is not valid, Is what is measured by it not false? In reality, emptiness; Meditating on it therefore becomes untenable.
examples.sa: प्रमाणमप्रमाणं चेन्ननु तत्प्रमितं मृषा। तत्त्वतः शून्यता तस्माद्भावानां नोपपद्यते॥

examples.dm: By renouncing everything, one transcends suffering, And my mind seeks to achieve that transcendence; Since I must give everything away at once, It is best to give it to all sentient beings.
examples.gm: By giving up everything, nirvana is attained, And my mind seeks to accomplish nirvana. Since I must part with everything at once, It is best given to sentient beings.
examples.sa: सर्वत्यागश्च निर्वाणं निर्वाणार्थि च मे मनः। त्यक्तव्यं चेन्मया सर्वं वरं सत्त्वेषु दीयताम्॥

examples.dm: If the root of the teaching is the monkhood itself, Then even being a monk is a difficult state to maintain. For those whose minds are still directed toward objects, Even nirvana is a difficult state to maintain.
examples.gm: If being a monk is the root of the teaching, Even being a monk is difficult to establish. For those whose minds have apprehension, Even nirvāṇa is difficult to establish.
examples.sa: शासनं भिक्षुतामूलं भिक्षुतैव च दुःस्थिता। सावलम्बनचित्तानां निर्वाणमपि दुःस्थितम्॥

examples.dm: When the object of analysis is thoroughly analyzed, There is no basis remaining for the analysis. Because there is no basis, it does not arise, And that is described as nirvana.
examples.gm: If the object of analysis has been analyzed, There is no basis for analysis. Because there is no basis, it does not arise, And that too is expressed as nirvāṇa.
examples.sa: विचारिते विचार्ये तु विचारस्यास्ति नाश्रयः। निराश्रितत्वान्नोदेति तच्च निर्वाणमुच्यते॥

examples.dm: For the sake of my desires, I have experienced Being burned and so forth in the hells thousands of times, Yet I have accomplished neither my own benefit Nor the benefit of others.
examples.gm: For the sake of desires, burning and so forth, I have experienced in hell thousands of times, but I did not accomplish my own benefit, Nor did I accomplish the benefit of others.
examples.sa: कोपार्थमेवमेवाहं नरकेषु सहस्रशः। कारितोऽस्मि न चात्मार्थः परार्थो वा कृतो मया॥

examples.dm: What need is there to say more? Observe the difference between these two: The childish who work for their own sake, And the Sages who work for the sake of others.
examples.gm: What need is there to say much? Childish beings act for their own purpose, and The Sage acts for the purpose of others. Look at the difference between these two!
examples.sa: बहुना वा किमुक्तेन दृश्यतामिदमन्तरम्। स्वार्थार्थिनश्च बालस्य मुनेश्चान्यार्थकारिणः॥

examples.dm: Furthermore, abandon the thought that you still have your own interests; I have sold you to others. Do not be distressed, but offer up your service.
examples.gm: "I still have my own purpose"— Cast away that thought which thinks it exists! Since I have sold you to others, Do not feel sorrow, offer your services.
examples.sa: अद्याप्यस्ति मम स्वार्थ इत्याशां त्यज सांप्रतम्। त्वं विक्रीतो मयान्येषु बहुखेदमचिन्तयन्॥

examples.dm: Even the direct perception of forms and so forth Exists by worldly renown, not by valid cognition. This is as false as the common renown Of purity in things that are actually impure.
examples.gm: Even the direct perception of forms and so forth Is through convention, not through valid cognition. That is false, just like the convention Of being clean and so forth regarding what is unclean and so forth.
examples.sa: प्रत्यक्षमपि रूपादि प्रसिद्ध्या न प्रमाणतः। अशुच्यादिषु शुच्यादिप्रसिद्धिरिव सा मृषा॥

examples.dm: If that knowledge exists even in the world, Why is it not seen? If the world is not a valid authority, Then even seeing what is manifest is not true.
examples.gm: That knowledge is also in the world; Since it exists, why is it not seen? If the world is not a valid cognition, Seeing the manifest is also not true.
examples.sa: लोकस्यापि च तज्ज्ञानमस्ति कस्मान्न पश्यति। लोकाप्रमाणतायां चेत् व्यक्तदर्शनमप्यसत्॥

examples.dm: If a valid authority is not valid, Would that which is measured by it not be false? In that case, the meditation On emptiness would be untenable.
examples.gm: If valid cognition is not valid, Is what is measured by it not false? In reality, emptiness; Meditating on it therefore becomes untenable.
examples.sa: प्रमाणमप्रमाणं चेन्ननु तत्प्रमितं मृषा। तत्त्वतः शून्यता तस्माद्भावानां नोपपद्यते॥

examples.dm: Upon all the jewels of the sublime Dharma, And upon the reliquaries and the sacred images, May a rain of precious flowers and the like Fall in a continuous, uninterrupted stream.
examples.gm: Upon all the rare and supreme holy Dharma, Stūpas, and images, May a rain of jewels, flowers, and the like, Fall without interruption.
examples.sa: सर्वसद्धर्मरत्नेषु चैत्येषु प्रतिमासु च। पुष्परत्नादिवर्षाश्च प्रवर्तन्तां निरन्तरम्॥

examples.dm: Toward those who revile and destroy Sacred images, stupas, and the sublime Dharma, It is not appropriate for me to feel hatred, For the Buddhas and the like cannot be harmed.
examples.gm: Towards images, stupas, and the sublime Dharma, Even if someone disparages or destroys them, It is inappropriate for me to have anger, For the Buddhas and so forth suffer no harm.
examples.sa: प्रतिमास्तूपसद्धर्मनाशकाक्रोशकेषु च। न युज्यते मम द्वेषो बुद्धादीनां न हि व्यथा॥

examples.dm: Therefore, just as I have vowed, I must respectfully fulfill it. If I do not make an effort from this moment on, I shall sink lower and lower.
examples.gm: Therefore, just as I have promised, I shall respectfully accomplish it. If from today I do not make effort, I will go lower and lower.
examples.sa: तस्माद्यथाप्रतिज्ञातं साधनीयं मयादरात्। नाद्य चेत्क्रियते यत्नस्तलेनास्मि तलं गतः॥

examples.dm: Even many who possess learning and faith, And who apply themselves with great diligence, Become defiled by the stain of downfalls, Due to the fault of lacking introspective awareness.
examples.gm: Those who are learned and have faith, And many who dedicate themselves to effort, Because they incur the fault of lacking introspection, Will become tainted by downfalls.
examples.sa: अनेके श्रुतवन्तोऽपि श्राद्धा यत्नपरा अपि। असंप्रजन्यदोषेण भवन्त्यापत्तिकश्मलाः॥

examples.dm: If one protects a wound out of fear of even its slight pain, Then why, fearing the crushing of the Samghāta and Raurava hells, Does one not guard the wound of the mind?
examples.gm: Because of the minor suffering of a wound, If one who is afraid carefully protects the wound, Those who fear the Crushing and Destroying Hells, Why do they not guard the wound of the mind?
examples.sa: व्रणदुःखलवाद्भीतो रक्षामि व्रणमादरात्। संघातपर्वताघाताद्भीतश्चित्तव्रणं न किम्॥

examples.dm: May those heaps of glowing coals become heaps of jewels; May the scorched earth be spread as a crystal floor; May the mountains of the Crushing Hell also become Celestial palaces of offerings, filled with Sugatas.
examples.gm: May those heaps of coal become heaps of jewels. May the burning ground be paved as a crystal ground. May the mountains of the Crushing Hell also, of offerings Become immeasurable palaces, filled with Sugatas.
examples.sa: सोऽङ्गारराशिर्मणिराशिरस्तु तप्ता च भूः स्फाटिककुट्टिमं स्यात्। भवन्तु संघातमहीधराश्च पूजाविमानाः सुगतप्रपूर्णाः॥

examples.dm: If you think, "I shall live on my gains And, while doing so, exhaust my sins and perform merit," Yet you become angry for the sake of that gain, Will your merit not be exhausted and will you not incur sin?
examples.gm: If you say, "By living on account of gains, I will exhaust negative actions and perform merit," If I become angry for the sake of gains, Will not merit be exhausted and negative actions created?
examples.sa: पापक्षयं च पुण्यं च लाभाज्जीवन् करोमि चेत्। पुण्यक्षयश्च पापं च लाभार्थं क्रुध्यतो ननु॥

examples.dm: Some commit misdeeds out of delusion; If others, being deluded, become angry, Who among them is without fault, And who is the one who is at fault?
examples.gm: Some commit faults through ignorance, And some, being ignorant, become angry. Among them, who is to be considered faultless? And who is to be considered at fault?
examples.sa: मोहादेकेऽपराध्यन्ति कुप्यन्त्यन्ये विमोहिताः। ब्रूमः कमेषु निर्दोषं कम वा ब्रूमोऽपराधिनम्॥

examples.dm: With their skin entirely flayed by the henchmen of Yama, they are utterly tormented, And molten copper, melted by a searing fire, is poured over their bodies; Pierced by flaming swords and spears until their flesh is torn into hundreds of pieces, They fall upon the intensely blazing iron ground as a result of their many non-virtues.
examples.gm: Utterly tormented by the henchmen of Yama stripping away one's skin entirely, Molten copper melted by intensely hot fire poured onto one's body, Pierced by blazing swords and short spears, one's flesh scattered in a hundred pieces, Through many unwholesome deeds, one falls onto a ground of intensely blazing iron.
examples.sa: यमपुरुषापनीतसकलच्छविरार्तरवो हुतवहतापविद्रुतकताम्रनिषिक्ततनुः। ज्वलदसिशक्तिघातशतशातितमांसदलःपतति सुतप्तलोहधरणीष्वशुभैर्बहुशः॥

examples.dm: If one associates with the childish, then from such childishness, Self-praise, the disparagement of others, And talk that delights in cyclic existence and the like, All manner of non-virtue will certainly arise.
examples.gm: If one associates with the childish, Praising oneself and disparaging others, And talking about the joys of cyclic existence and so forth, Non-virtue will certainly arise in every way.
examples.sa: आत्मोत्कर्षः परावर्णः संसाररतिसंकथा। इत्याद्यवश्यमशुभं किंचिद्बालस्य बालतः॥

examples.dm: The conventional and the ultimate: These are held to be the two truths. The ultimate is not an object of the intellect; The intellect is said to be the conventional.
examples.gm: The relative and the ultimate— These are asserted to be the two truths. The ultimate is not the domain of the intellect; The intellect is said to be the relative.
examples.sa: संवृतिः परमार्थश्च सत्यद्वयमिदं मतम्। बुद्धेरगोचरस्तत्त्वं बुद्धिः संवृतिरुच्यते॥

examples.dm: Nowhere is there any single condition That has the power to produce everything. If ultimate reality is nirvana And cyclic existence is the conventional, then
examples.gm: That a single condition has the capacity for everything Nowhere exists. "If the ultimate is nirvāṇa, And saṃsāra is the relative, in that case,
examples.sa: नैकस्य सर्वसामर्थ्यं प्रत्ययस्यास्ति कुत्रचित्। निर्वृतः परमार्थेन संवृत्या यदि संसरेत्॥

examples.dm: If you ask what created the variety of causes, It is from the very variety of preceding causes. Why is a cause able to produce an effect? It is from the very power of the preceding cause.
examples.gm: If one asks, what made the variations of causes? From the variations of prior causes themselves. Why are causes able to produce effects? From the power of prior causes themselves.
examples.sa: किंकृतो हेतुभेदश्चेत् पूर्वहेतुप्रभेदतः। कस्माच्चेत्फलदो हेतुः पूर्वहेतुप्रभावतः॥

examples.dm: Then even if you do not wish it, The arising of a manifest state from what was non-existent remains a fact. If the effect exists within the cause, Then one who eats food would be eating filth.
examples.gm: The arising of what is unmanifest Remains, even though you do not assert it. If the result abides in the cause, One who eats food would eat excrement.
examples.sa: व्यक्तस्यासत उत्पत्तिरकामस्यापि ते स्थिता। अन्नादोऽमेध्यभक्षः स्यात् फलं हेतौ यदि स्थितम्॥

examples.dm: Since the sole Guide of beings, through his immeasurable intellect, Has thoroughly examined it and seen its great value, Those who wish to escape the realms of cyclic existence Should firmly grasp this precious awakening mind.
examples.gm: Since the sole captain of beings, with limitless intellect, Has thoroughly examined it and found it to be highly precious, Those who wish to be separated from the states of wandering Should perfectly and firmly hold the precious mind of awakening.
examples.sa: सुपरीक्षितमप्रमेयधीभि-र्बहुमूल्यं जगदेकसार्थवाहैः। गतिपत्तनविप्रवासशीलाःसुदृढं गृह्णत बोधिचित्तरत्नम्॥

examples.dm: To the Victors and their spiritual heirs, I offer my entire body forever. O Supreme Beings, please accept me completely; With devotion, I shall become your servant.
examples.gm: To the Conquerors and their Children, I Offer my entire body forever. Supreme Beings, please accept me completely; With devotion I will become your subject.
examples.sa: ददामि चात्मानमहं जिनेभ्यः सर्वेण सर्वं च तदात्मजेभ्यः। परिग्रहं मे कुरुताग्रसत्त्वा युष्मासु दासत्वमुपैमि भक्त्या॥

examples.dm: To all the Buddhas of the three times, And to the Dharma and the Supreme Assembly, With as many bodies as there are atoms in the realms, I bow down and pay homage.
examples.gm: To all the Buddhas who have gone in the three times, Along with the Dharma and the Supreme Assembly, With bodies as numerous as all the atoms in the fields, Bowing down, I pay homage.
examples.sa: सर्वक्षेत्राणुसंख्यैश्च प्रणामैः प्रणमाम्यहम्। सर्वत्र्यध्वगतान् बुद्धान् सहधर्मगणोत्तमान्॥

examples.dm: If one must remain cautious Even at a small, ordinary precipice, What need is there to mention the long-lasting abyss That falls for a thousand leagues?
examples.gm: Even on a small, ordinary precipice, If one must remain careful, Of falling a thousand yojanas On a long-lasting precipice, what need to mention?
examples.sa: अत्यप्रमत्तस्तिष्ठामि प्रपातेष्वितरेष्वपि। किमु योजनसाहस्रे प्रपाते दीर्घकालिके॥

examples.dm: Just as the great elements, such as earth, And like space itself, may I always be The basis for the various means of subsistence For immeasurable sentient beings.
examples.gm: Just like earth and the other great elements, And like space, permanently, For limitless sentient beings, May I also be the ground of manifold sustenance.
examples.sa: पृथिव्यादीनि भूतानि निःशेषाकाशवासिनाम्। सत्त्वानामप्रमेयाणां यथाभोगान्यनेकधा॥

examples.dm: Even if all the gods and demigods Were to rise up against me as enemies, They would be unable to lead me into Or cast me into the fires of the Avīci hell.
examples.gm: Even if the gods and demigods All rose up against me as enemies, Even they would not be able To lead and place me in the fire of Avīci.
examples.sa: सर्वे देवा मनुष्याश्च यदि स्युर्मम शत्रवः। तेऽपि नावीचिकं वह्निं समुदानयितुं क्षमाः॥

examples.dm: Therefore, I shall firmly grasp And properly guard this mind of mine. Apart from the ascetic discipline of guarding the mind, What is the use of many other disciplines?
examples.gm: Therefore, this mind of mine, I shall hold it well and guard it well. Except for the discipline of guarding the mind, What is the use of many disciplines?
examples.sa: तस्मात्स्वधिष्ठितं चित्तं मया कार्यं सुरक्षितम्। चित्तरक्षाव्रतं मुक्त्त्वा बहुभिः किं मम व्रतैः॥

examples.dm: If one desires gain, honor, or fame, Or if one seeks a circle of attendants, Or if one's mind desires to be served, At those times, one should remain like a log of wood.
examples.gm: Desiring gain, honor, and fame, Or desiring to seek attendants and retinues, If one's mind desires to be served, At that time, one should remain like a piece of wood.
examples.sa: लाभसत्कारकीर्त्यर्थि परिवारार्थि वा पुनः। उपस्थानार्थे मे चित्तं तस्मात्तिष्ठामि काष्ठवत्॥

examples.dm: Regarding the body as a boat, a mere support for coming and going, Think of it as a vessel, And in order to accomplish the welfare of sentient beings, Transform it into a wish-fulfilling body.
examples.gm: Merely as a support for going and coming, Conceive of the body as a boat, and In order to accomplish the welfare of sentient beings, Transform it into a wish-fulfilling body.
examples.sa: काये नौबुद्धिमाधाय गत्यागमननिश्रयात्॥ यथाकामंगमं कायं कुरु सत्त्वार्थसिद्धये॥

examples.dm: The causes of happiness occur only occasionally, While the causes of suffering are extremely numerous. Without suffering, there is no renunciation; Therefore, O mind, remain steadfast.
examples.gm: The causes of happiness occur sometimes; The causes of suffering are very many. Without suffering, there is no renunciation. Therefore, mind, resolve to be steadfast!
examples.sa: कथंचिल्लभ्यते सौख्यं दुःखं स्थितमयत्नतः। दुःखेनैव च निःसारः चेतस्तस्माद् दृढीभव॥

examples.dm: This happiness of your rejoicing Is a source of bliss that is blameless; It is permitted by those endowed with excellence, And is the supreme way of attracting others.
examples.gm: This joy of your rejoicing Produces happiness and has no blame; It is approved by those possessing good qualities, And is also supreme in gathering others.
examples.sa: इदं च ते हृष्टिसुखं निरवद्यं सुखोदयम्। न वारितं च गुणिभिः परावर्जनमुत्तमम्॥

examples.dm: Since it was accomplished by both him and me, The fruit of this patience Should be offered to him first, For in this way, he is the cause of patience.
examples.gm: Since it is accomplished by this one and myself, Therefore, the fruit of patience Should first be offered to them, For they are the cause of patience.
examples.sa: मया चानेन चोपात्तं तस्मादेतत् क्षमाफलम्। एतस्मै प्रथमं देयमेतत्पूर्वा क्षमा यतः॥

examples.dm: Through savoring the taste of idle pleasure, And the craving that relies on sleep, One does not feel weariness for the suffering of cyclic existence; From these, laziness fully arises.
examples.gm: Tasting the pleasure of idleness, and Craving that relies on sleep; From feeling no weariness toward the sufferings of saṃsāra, Laziness comes to arise.
examples.sa: अव्यापारसुखास्वादनिद्रापाश्रयतृष्णया। संसारदुःखानुद्वेगादालस्यमुपजायते॥

examples.dm: Thus, having abandoned the opposing factors, One should strive to increase diligence through the powers of aspiration, pride, joy, relinquishment, Earnest application, and mastery.
examples.gm: Thus, having abandoned the discordant factors, Through aspiration, pride, joy, and relinquishment, And the powers of earnest application and mastery, I should strive to increase joyful endeavor.
examples.sa: एवं विपक्षमुन्मूल्य यतेतोत्साहवृद्धये। छन्दमानरतित्यागतात्पर्यवशिताबलैः॥

examples.dm: Just as one carrying a vessel filled with mustard oil, Followed by a man with a drawn sword threatening to kill him, Is terrified of spilling it, so should the practitioner be focused.
examples.gm: Just as one carrying a vessel filled with mustard oil, With a sword-bearer standing nearby, Fearing the threat of death if it spills, An ascetic should likewise exert himself.
examples.sa: तैलपात्रधरो यद्वदसिहस्तैरधिष्ठितः। स्खलिते मरणत्रासात्तत्परः स्यात्तथा व्रती॥

examples.dm: If there are others who disparage me, What reason is there for me to be pleased by praise? If there are others who praise me, What reason is there for me to be displeased by disparagement?
examples.gm: If there are others who disparage me, What joy is there for me in praise? If there are others who praise me, What displeasure is there in disparagement?
examples.sa: मामेवान्ये जुगुप्सन्ति किं प्रहृष्याम्यहं स्तुतः। मामेवान्ये प्रशंसन्ति किं विषीदामि निन्दितः॥

examples.dm: You do not desire even a tiny worm That arises from filth, Yet you desire a body that is a mass of many impurities And was likewise born from filth.
examples.gm: A filth-worm arisen from filth, Even a tiny one, you do not desire, Yet a body whose nature is much filth, And born of filth, you desire.
examples.sa: अमेध्यभवमल्पत्वान्न वाञ्छस्यशुचिं कृमिम्। बह्वमेध्यमयं कायममेध्यजमपीच्छसि॥

examples.dm: Thinking, "If I give this away, what will I have to enjoy?" Is the way of a demon, thinking only of one's own benefit. Thinking, "If I use this myself, what will I have to give?" Is the Dharma of the gods, thinking of the welfare of others.
examples.gm: "If I give, what will I consume?"— Thinking of one's own purpose is the way of a demon. "If I consume, what will I give?"— Thinking of others' purpose is the quality of a deity.
examples.sa: यदि दास्यामि किं भोक्ष्ये इत्यात्मार्थे पिशाचता। यदि भोक्ष्ये किं ददामीति परार्थे देवराजता॥

examples.dm: This concludes the eighth chapter, titled "The Explanation of Meditative Concentration," from the *Entering the Conduct of a Bodhisattva*.
examples.gm: From Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva, the eighth chapter, called The Teaching on Meditative Concentration.

examples.dm: Whatever is seen, heard, or known, Is not what is to be negated here; What is to be overturned here is the conceptualization of them as true, Which is the cause of suffering.
examples.gm: How things are seen, heard, and known Is not to be refuted here; Here, what becomes the cause of suffering, The conceptualization of true existence, is to be reversed.
examples.sa: यथा दृष्टं श्रुतं ज्ञातं नैवेह प्रतिषिध्यते। सत्यतः कल्पना त्वत्र दुःखहेतुर्निवार्यते॥

examples.dm: If you say it is because the Mahāyāna is contested, Since your own scriptures are contested by non-Buddhists, And other scriptures are contested by your own and other schools, They would also have to be rejected because they are contested.
examples.gm: If you say the Mahāyāna is subject to dispute, The scriptures are disputed by non-Buddhists, And other scriptures are disputed by ourselves and others; Since they are subject to dispute, they would have to be discarded.
examples.sa: सविवादं महायानमिति चेदागमं त्यज। तीर्थिकैः सविवादत्वात्स्वैः परैश्चागमान्तरम्॥

examples.dm: As long as the collection of conditions remains, The body appears like a person; Likewise, as long as the hands and so forth are present, The body will appear to exist therein.
examples.gm: As long as the collection of conditions lasts, The body appears like a person. Likewise, as long as it is present in the hands and so forth, For that long, the body appears there.
examples.sa: यावत्प्रत्ययसामग्री तावत्कायः पुमानिव। एवं करादौ सा यावत्तावत्कायोऽत्र दृश्यते॥

examples.dm: Īśvara is not space, because space is inert; He is not the self, as that has already been refuted. And if the creator is also inconceivable, What is the point of speaking of him as "inconceivable"?
examples.gm: Īśvara is not space, because it is devoid of movement; He is not the self, because it was already refuted before; And as for a creator who is inconceivable, What is the use of speaking of the inconceivable?
examples.sa: नाकाशमीशोऽचेष्टत्वात् नात्मा पूर्वनिषेधतः। अचिन्त्यस्य च कर्तृत्वमप्यचिन्त्यं किमुच्यते॥

examples.dm: Thus, there is no cessation, And likewise, there is no existence. Therefore, all these wandering beings Are eternally unborn and unceasing.
examples.gm: Thus, there is no cessation, And there is no entity; therefore, All these migrating beings Are always unproduced and unceased.
examples.sa: एवं न च निरोधोऽस्ति न च भावोऽस्ति सर्वदा। अजातमनिरुद्धं च तस्मात्सर्वमिदं जगत्॥

examples.dm: May those submerged in the fordless river, which is like a pit of fire, Their flesh all decayed and their skeletons the color of white kunda flowers, Attain celestial bodies through the power of my merit, And dwell with goddesses by the gently flowing waters.
examples.gm: May those sinking in the unfordable river that is like a fire pit, Their flesh all destroyed, with bones the color of jasmine flowers, By the power of my virtue attain the bodies of gods, And abide together with goddesses in the Mandākinī.
examples.sa: पतितसकलमांसाः कुन्दवर्णास्थिदेहा दहनसमजलायां वैतरण्यां निमग्नाः। मम कुशलबलेन प्राप्तदिव्यात्मभावाः सह सुरवनिताभिः सन्तु मन्दाकिनीस्थाः॥

examples.dm: In all the various circles of retinues, May many Bodhisattvas Dwell, having adorned the surface of the earth With their own excellence.
examples.gm: In all the circles of retinues that exist, May many bodhisattvas Adorn the surface of the earth with their excellence, And remain dwelling there.
examples.sa: बोधिसत्त्वमहापर्षन्मण्डलानि समन्ततः। निषीदन्तु स्वशोभाभिर्मण्डयन्तु महीतलम्॥

examples.dm: May I be sustained and live, Even on a diet of the simplest food. In all my lives, may I obtain Perfect circumstances for living in solitude.
examples.gm: May I, even with simple food, Live endowed with vitality. In all my lifetimes, May I attain the perfection of solitary places.
examples.sa: येन तेनासनेनाहं यापयेयं बलान्वितः। विवेकवाससामग्रीं प्राप्नुयां सर्वजातिषु॥
